history.title: Depot Wall Charger Capacity

style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: Architectural photograph at blue hour, wide asymmetric composition with heavy editorial framing on the left. An industrial electrical service panel mounted on a weathered corrugated steel depot wall, with a thick, heavy-duty charging umbilical cable routing out to an unbranded modern electric delivery van parked in the shadows. Shot with a 35mm anamorphic wide lens with dramatic falloff. Deep blue ambient light contrasted by a single warm amber worklight illuminating the metallic conduit and the brushed steel of the service box. Crisp crystalline air, clean high-contrast atmosphere, quiet confidence, editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, people, faces, humans, generic office worker
rationale: The architectural night treatment perfectly captures the reality of fleet charging: vehicles sitting plugged into a depot wall overnight, governed by the facility's electrical capacity under the cool glow of industrial worklights.
subject: an industrial electrical service panel and heavy charging umbilical connected to a parked electric delivery van
core_thesis: A delivery fleet's electric charging constraint and cost are fundamentally dictated by the depot's physical power infrastructure, not the vehicle's maximum capability.
core_conflict: The mismatch between high-capacity electric delivery vans and the hard limits of depot wall service panels and circuits.
composition: wide asymmetric composition with heavy editorial framing on the left
